key_insight: Deep learning of retinal fluorescence lifetime maps modestly distinguished type 2 diabetes status, outperforming an age-only classifier.
clinical_relevance: This diabetes imaging study—not cancer drug discovery—suggests retinal fluorescence may capture diabetes-associated metabolic signals, but does not establish clinical screening utility.
method: Generated corrected mean fluorescence lifetime maps from FLIO scans.
Compared CNN, ResNet-18, and XGBoost models for three-class and binary glycemic classification.
Tested age-adjusted group differences and compared FLIO models with age-only and combined models.
evidence_signal: In 1,783 participants, the FLIO CNN achieved AUROC 0.60 ± 0.04 for three-class classification and 0.67 ± 0.04 for normal versus diabetic classification; adding age did not improve performance.
watch_item: Modest discrimination and a cross-sectional design limit clinical interpretation; external validation is needed before screening use.
paper_title: Deep Learning of Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Ophthalmoscopy for Type 2 Diabetes Classification
